newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy recovering despite slowdown--EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy recovering despite slowdown--EPA.

text.p: Japan's government maintained a guardedly optimistic assessment of the economy in its monthly economic report released on Tuesday, saying the economy is recovering despite a temporary slowdown caused by the effects of a sales tax rise in April.

"We have kept our overall assessment of the economy unchanged in that we see the economy continuing to recover despite a temporary slowdown in the pace of recovery," a senior official of the government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) told reporters.
The pace of the recovery was slowing temporarily, but the economy was continuing its recovery led by firm private demand, the EPA's monthly report said.

The official who briefed reporters said negative effects of the sales tax increase were still seen in July. "We thought the negative impact would disappear in the April-June period, so we still need to see when such effects will vanish," he said.
The report also said housing construction remained weak in reaction to brisk construction activity that took place before the sales tax was raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
In its report last month, the EPA said housing construction was at a high level, given the continuation of low interest rates.
"Private consumption is on a slow recovery trend although negative effects of the sales tax increase were still seen," the report said.
The official said the economy could be back on a firm recovery track after the negative effects of the sales tax increase disappeared.
"Basically, the Japanese economy is becoming firmer, heading for a self-sustainable recovery," he said.
Behind the optimistic view are increases in incomes and employment, he added.
